rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test the most critical design decision: multimodal integration. This configuration tests combining RNA (pca_n2000) and image (resnet50) data with simple concatenation fusion, establishing a baseline for multimodal performance. It directly addresses whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines, which is foundational for subsequent exploration of more complex fusion methods or encoder choices.

The existing evidence from config_016 shows a multimodal setup with concat fusion achieves 0.5266 validation accuracy. This experiment tests the same model setting but with weighted fusion instead of concat, directly comparing fusion strategies. It clarifies whether weighted fusion improves performance, a critical design choice with sparse evidence, while staying within the same model architecture to isolate the impact of fusion method.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with pca_n2000 and resnet50 achieve ~0.526 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a stronger image encoder) to determine if this improves performance, clarifying the importance of image encoder choice. It directly addresses a key design decision with potential for significant impact, while building on the existing multimodal singleprofile baseline.

The existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l as the image encoder (config_022) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.5353) so far. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_023) improves performance with the same encoder, clarifying the impact of fusion methods. It is the best use of the next experiment as it directly builds on the current best configuration, exploring a critical design choice (fusion type) with minimal deviation from proven components.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with concat fusion (config_022) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.5353). This experiment tests whether switching to scvi_n200 RNA encoder while maintaining the same image encoder and aggregation method (avgpool) could improve performance, clarifying the impact of RNA encoder choice on multimodal multiprofile models.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l encoders (config_036) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.715). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (a more complex method) improves performance, clarifying the importance of aggregation strategy. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design choice (aggregation) in the current top-performing configuration.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, and transformer aggregation (config_038) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion (config_039) improves performance, clarifying the importance of fusion strategies. It is a logical extension of the current top-performing setup, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_039) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using scgpt as the RNA encoder (instead of scvi_n200) in this high-performing setup could further improve accuracy. It addresses the critical design choice of RNA encoder while leveraging the already validated aggregation and fusion strategies, balancing exploration and exploitation.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile setups with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion, which could clarify whether the choice of RNA encoder (scvi_n200 vs scgpt) and fusion method (concat vs weighted) significantly impacts performance. It directly addresses uncertainty about the relative effectiveness of these components in the multimodal multiprofile setting.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieve high accuracy (config_039: 0.725), but singleprofile models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (config_034) have not been tested. This experiment tests whether removing aggregation (None) and using concat fusion in singleprofile with scvi_n200 improves performance compared to previous singleprofile models (e.g., config_022: 0.535). It clarifies the impact of aggregation and RNA encoder choices, balancing exploration of promising RNA encoders with exploitation of high-performing components.
